problem: Index native lexeme is XML-encoded; native SAX callback title is decoded XML character data. Comparing different representations can reject an otherwise exact page identity.
scope: Raw index DB, row/page IDs, UTF8 title lexemes, ordinal/group offsets, raw lines and hashes remain immutable. Derive a separate semantic expected-title value once for comparison/transcript, retain both exact representations with helper/source pins.
decoder: Only5 XML predefined entities plus XML1.0 decimal/#x hexadecimal character references; strict UTF8/XML scalar validity. No HTML5 unknown names/repair, case-fold, NFC, underscore replacement, trimming/collapse or recursive unescape. LiteralCR/LF explicitly held as unsupported line-index representation rather than silently normalized; references to XML-valid whitespace preserve their scalar. Max64KiB UTF8 is a resource cap, never a quality threshold.
downstream_integration_proposed: Keep sink ordered page-ID and exact semantic-title equality. No fuzzy/threshold relaxation.
Use semantic expected-title in both sink expected tuples and frozen-index identity transcript; keep raw lexeme/rawline SHA256 sidecar and decoder pin.
Do not mutate the verified complete index DB or raw selection packet.
Require exact actual targetgroup diagnostic proof and new isolated calibration profile/pins independently reviewed before any actual calibration rerun.
Any invalid/unsupported lexeme is a terminal hold, no skip/replacement.
